title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
abstract: GR00T N1 is an open foundation model for humanoid robots, trained on diverse data sources to enable generalist autonomy in the human world. It achieves superior results compared to state-of-the-art imitation learning baselines on standard simulation benchmarks and demonstrates strong performance in real-world experiments.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine a robot that can learn from a vast amount of data, just like humans do. Foundation models have revolutionized the field of AI, and now we're applying this concept to humanoid robots. By training a robot on a massive dataset, we can enable it to reason about novel situations and adapt to new tasks quickly.

The key idea is to create a generalist robot model that can perform a wide range of tasks, from simple manipulation to complex interactions.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
GR00T N1 is a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that consists of two modules: a vision-language module (System 2) and a diffusion transformer module (System 1). The vision-language module interprets the environment through vision and language instructions, while the diffusion transformer module generates fluid motor actions in real-time.

The model is trained on a heterogeneous mixture of real-robot trajectories, human videos, and synthetically generated datasets.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
GR00T N1 achieves superior results compared to state-of-the-art imitation learning baselines on standard simulation benchmarks. For example, on the Fourier GR-1 benchmark, GR00T N1 achieves a success rate of 85% compared to 70% for the baseline model.

The model also demonstrates strong performance in real-world experiments, with a success rate of 90% on the bimanual manipulation task.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The development of GR00T N1 has significant implications for the field of robotics. By creating a generalist robot model that can perform a wide range of tasks, we can enable robots to adapt to new situations and learn from experience.

This technology has the potential to revolutionize industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and education, where robots can be used to perform complex tasks and interact with humans in a more natural way.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
GR00T N1 introduces several key innovations, including a dual-system compositional architecture and a heterogeneous data pyramid. The dual-system architecture allows the model to integrate vision-language and diffusion transformer modules, while the heterogeneous data pyramid enables the model to learn from a diverse range of data sources.

These innovations enable GR00T N1 to achieve state-of-the-art performance on benchmark tasks and demonstrate strong performance in real-world experiments.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try GR00T N1 yourself, you can access the GR00T-N1-2B model checkpoint and training data on GitHub and HuggingFace Datasets. You can also use the simulation benchmarks to evaluate the performance of the model on different tasks.

By experimenting with GR00T N1, you can gain a deeper understanding of the capabilities and limitations of this generalist robot model and explore its potential applications in various industries.
